top_story.headline: FEC presses Cory Booker's Senate campaign over a $9,178.33 'unauthorized transaction'
top_story.dek: An RFAI to the New Jersey senator's committee says the disbursement appears to be an unauthorized use of committee funds.
paragraphs: The Federal Election Commission sent an RFAI on October 21 to Cory Booker for Senate, the campaign committee of Sen. Cory A. Booker (D-NJ). It asks about a Schedule B disbursement on Line 21 described as 'Unauthorized transaction,' totaling $9,178.33. The disbursement appears on the committee's amended Year-End 2025 report, which the FEC received on July 1, 2026.

The letter says the transaction 'appears to be related to an apparent unauthorized disbursement of Committee funds.' It also says the Commission 'notes your explanation of the unauthorized activity,' and asks for any additional information as it becomes available. That explanation is not in the filing text, so what happened is not stated. The letter warns the Commission may still take further legal action over the apparent improper use of committee funds. The treasurer is Scott Kobler, and the response is due November 25.

Also filed this week: Harris County Democratic Party told the FEC that 42 receipts totaling $148,176 meant for state or nonfederal activity were mistakenly deposited into its federal account. That statement is covered in the Form 99 section.

sections.headline: Booker's disbursement query leads five filings tied to sitting lawmakers
paragraphs: Three incumbents received RFAIs: Sen. Cory A. Booker over an unauthorized disbursement, and Reps. Lance Gooden and Shri Thanedar over excessive contributions and incomplete donor identification. Rep. Keith Self filed a short Form 99, and a committee tagged to Christopher C. Collins filed a termination.

items: FEC asks Sen. Cory A. Booker (D-NJ)'s campaign to say more about a $9,178.33 'Unauthorized transaction' it calls an apparent improper use of committee funds. The letter notes the committee's earlier explanation and asks for more as it becomes available. Treasurer is Scott Kobler. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

FEC asks Rep. Lance Gooden (R-TX) to address contributions that appear to exceed the limits and donors listed with 'blank/blank' employer and occupation. The letter also says the committee ID listed for the Association of Equipment Manufacturers (C30003511) appears to be incorrect. It concerns the amended July Quarterly report received 09/01. Treasurer is Robert Phillips III. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

FEC asks Rep. Shri Thanedar (D-MI) to address apparently excessive contributions and donors with unacceptable employer and occupation entries. Entries cited include 'Information Requested/Information Requested,' 'Owl Creek Asset Management/Information Requested,' 'Self/Business' and 'Self/Self Employed.' It concerns the July Quarterly report. The treasurer is Thanedar himself. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)
Rep. Keith Self (R-TX) tells the FEC a 48-hour report was filed to add a donor received through the earmark conduit WinRed. The statement says the PAC on the report was previously reported. (Form 99)
Christopher C. Collins (R-NY)'s committee, Collins for Congress, filed a termination approval. Terminations are not read for this newsletter. (Filing)

sections.headline: 48 RFAIs for non-incumbents, two-thirds of them missing-report notices
paragraphs: The FEC's October Quarterly follow-up cycle produced a large batch. 33 candidate committees got the same standard notice that the committee may have failed to file its report. The other 15 RFAIs are substantive, including three to Rolling Sea Action Fund that share a treasurer, Jason Hinton, care of Kalik and Associates Inc.

sections.headline: 25 Form 99s: loan paperwork from both Senate party committees, late-disclosure admissions and a $50 million license valuation
paragraphs: Most of these are one-line threshold statements from tiny campaigns, but several matter. NRSC and DSCC filed bank-loan paperwork. Harris County Democratic Party reported $148,176 of misdirected receipts. Three committees admitted late disclosures: BlueWaveAmerica, You Can Push Back and The Wisco Project PAC.

The red-flag scan flagged the NRSC filing on 'grand jury,' 'money launder' and 'theft.' Those hits come from standard boilerplate in the 127-page loan agreement (a jury-trial waiver, anti-terrorism and anti-money-laundering definitions, and an uninsured-loss clause). They are not findings about the committee.

items: NRSC files a Chain Bridge Bank credit facility raised from $17 million to $20 million. The package has a loan agreement dated 09/01/2026 and a first amendment dated 09/23/2026. It includes Schedule C-1 forms for $17,000,000 and $3,000,000 and lists deposit accounts and a donor list as collateral valued at $37,616,301. Treasurer is Kristi Broghamer. The FEC's record lists receipt 10/19. (Form 99)

ActBlue tells the FEC a vendor offset was moved to Line 17. It is income from Diamond Assets' purchase of computer equipment at fair market value. The filing answers a 09/23 RFAI on the April Monthly report. (Form 99)
Bishop Staten for Congress says it has received no funds and spent under $5,000. It says it remains eligible to keep filing this statement. (Form 99)

BlueWaveAmerica admits it reported a founder's loan and payments late and blames a miscommunication. The founder lent the money for a $76,000 annual NGP VAN/EveryAction contract and also paid Amazon Web Services and Google GSuite directly, around his medical emergency. The treasurer says she learned of it in August. The loan repayments were $2,626.22 and $150, and a third amendment was filed to fix a Line 29 error. This is a late disclosure by the filer's own account. It responds to a 10/01 RFAI. (Form 99)
Cinquemani for Congress says no loan agreement, loan forgiveness letter or debt settlement plan applies to it. Republican challenger Joseph Cinquemani, New York. (Form 99)
Committee for Ellis Colvin asks the FEC to terminate it. The Maryland 5th District candidate says he never raised or spent more than $5,000 and his candidacy ended with the June primary. (Form 99)
Deborah Ann Meidinger Hosey for US Congress says it has not met the $5,000 threshold for the 12-Day Pre-General report. No-party challenger, Florida. (Form 99)
DonHorn4Congress says it has neither spent nor raised $5,000. Republican challenger Don Horn, Texas. (Form 99)

DSCC files a Fourth Amendment raising its Amalgamated Bank facility from $20 million to $25 million. The maturity is extended to June 30, 2028. A Schedule C-1 shows a $15,000,000 draw and balance, with current and future assets as collateral valued at $25,000,000. The cover letter says the amendment was previously filed with the August Monthly and goes with the Pre-General C-1. Treasurer is Allison Wright. (Form 99)

Emmett White's committee files a 10-page Form 3 inside a Form 99 showing $62,568.09 in receipts and a matching $62,568.09 disbursement to himself. The sole itemized contributor is Lois Brown, dated 07/15/2025. The summary page shows $1,200 in operating expenditures, and the figures do not reconcile within the filing. A Schedule C-1 lists White as both lender and signer. The scan is partly garbled. The period is 09/01 to 09/22/2026. (Form 99)

Friends of Junaid says it refunded or redesignated general-election money after its candidate lost the primary. It answers a 09/15 letter that also cited an over-the-limit contribution, which it says was refunded. Candidate Junaid Ahmed (D) ran in the Illinois open seat. Treasurer is Victoria Perrone. Received 10/20. (Form 99)

Harris County Democratic Party says 42 receipts totaling $148,176 meant for state or nonfederal activity were mistakenly put into its federal account. They include $112,051 in 36 JJR contributions, $11,000 from three AuntieUp contributions, $125 tied to Christine Weems for Judge, a $15,000 AAPI-program wire and a $10,000 Annise Parker check. They are reported on Schedule A, Line 17 of the September Form 3X. The committee says it is taking corrective action. Received 10/20. (Form 99)
JimGrif4Congress26 says it has not met the $5,000 threshold and is not active. Republican challenger James Griffin, Connecticut. Received 10/20. (Form 99)
McCracken for Montana says it never passed $5,000 as of the October Quarterly close (09/30). Libertarian Patrick McCracken, Montana 2nd District. (Form 99)
McCracken for Montana says the same for the 12-Day Pre-General close (10/14). It was filed three minutes after the first statement. (Form 99)
Mel Tull for Congress says it has corrected its April and July Quarterly reports and resubmitted its termination. Democratic challenger Melvin Tull, Virginia. Treasurer is Kelsey Garnatz. (Form 99)

Ohio Democratic Party - Federal answers an August Monthly RFAI by amending its July Monthly cash on hand and adding the DSCC Victory Fund and Friends of State Parties to its Statement of Organization. It says the 'Consulting/Communications' payments were consulting fees, not public communications, and the printing did not name a clearly identified federal candidate. It responds to a 09/16 letter. (Form 99)
Ramon Mora for Congress says it has not met the $5,000 reporting threshold for the 2026 general election. Independent challenger, New Jersey. (Form 99)

SD PAC says apparently excessive contributions were a data entry error. They were reported as monetary contributions rather than other receipts in the non-contribution account. It says the noted committees are affiliated and the money was transfers. It filed an amended report and Statement of Organization. It responds to an August Monthly RFAI. Received 10/20. (Form 99)

Serrano for America says it has not passed $5,000 including the candidate's personal funds. It responds to an October Quarterly late notice and a 12-Day Pre-General reminder. Treasurer is Gerardo Serrano, a Kentucky House challenger. (Form 99)
Shurrun Daniel Campaign Committee says it has not reached the $5,000 filing threshold. Presidential candidate, South Carolina address. (Form 99)

State of Loc Nation for Clement for Senate restates a $50,250,000 valuation of an intellectual property license it reported as a candidate loan. The filing says the license is limited, non-exclusive and for campaign purposes, and ownership stays with Rev. Dr. Christina Loren Clement. The loan was reported on Form 3, Line 13(a), supported by a license dated 01/01/2026. The committee also received a missing-report notice (see RFAI section). (Form 99)

The Wisco Project PAC reports an untimely 48-hour notice for $1,055.78 in in-kind staff time supporting Mitchell Berman in Wisconsin's 1st District. The activity began in August, and the notice was filed 10/21, a late disclosure by its own account. It also cut a Rebecca Cooke (WI-03) in-kind estimate from $60,000 to $32,209 in an amended October Quarterly. The filing gives the original 48-hour notice date as 10/25/26, as written. (Form 99)
The Women's Cabinet says this hybrid PAC had no transactions in several periods. Those are Year-End 2025, both 2026 quarterlies and the 9/30/2026 filings. Received 10/20. (Form 99)

You Can Push Back admits filing 24-hour and 48-hour independent expenditure reports late. It blames miscommunication between consultants and its law firm and says everything was filed before the election. It also says its Netfile software coded expenditures with a non-FEC category, which it has amended. It responds to a 09/16 RFAI on the July Monthly. Received 10/20. (Form 99)
